Introducing Cube

Burak
25 min read
·
May 26, 2026

Cube is a virtual machine designed to enable trustless smart contract execution natively on Bitcoin.

The design space for Bitcoin programmability has been explored extensively over the past few years, with attempts ranging from sidechains and federations to rollups and covenants. Each comes with tradeoffs.

Cube takes a different approach by combining BitVM-style fraud proofs with a covenant-based execution model. The result is a system where any party can verify execution honestly without needing to trust an operator.

This document introduces the core architecture of Cube and explains the design choices that make it possible.

Architecture

At a high level, Cube is composed of three layers: the execution layer, the verification layer, and the settlement layer.

The execution layer is where smart contracts run. It is a deterministic virtual machine modeled after EVM-style execution, with adjustments for Bitcoin's transaction model.

The verification layer is where claims about execution correctness are checked. It uses BitVM-style fraud proofs to ensure that any invalid claim can be challenged and rejected on-chain.

The settlement layer is Bitcoin itself. Final state commitments are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain, providing the same security guarantees as base-layer Bitcoin transactions.
